arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Ms. Villa argued that reckless misdemeanors should be excluded from the phrase use of physical force.
Ms. Villa stated that this exclusion aligns with the Court's prior definitions of use.
Ms. Villa claimed that this view matches the common law definition of battery.
Ms. Eisenstein argued that Congress intended to keep guns away from assault and battery convicts.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: Federal law bans gun ownership for people convicted of assault or battery. The phrase use of physical force defines these crimes. The lower court ruled that reckless touching meets this definition. the side that brought the case argues that only intentional force counts. The government argues that any force, including reckless acts, fits the law.

paragraphs: This case defines the scope of federal gun bans. It determines which criminal convictions trigger lifetime firearm restrictions. It affects how states prosecute assault and battery. It clarifies the legal meaning of physical force in federal statutes. It impacts public safety and individual rights.
